built.summary:
Stream B (Books) is done, and all three findings are fixed. No earlier partial edits from this stream were in the tree. The existing diffs in accounting/routes.ts, orderPosting.ts and orders/service.ts belonged to other streams; I worked on top of them and reverted nothing.

(1) BOOKS-R2-01, three parts:
- Period close: POST /accounting/period-close now refuses today with 422 LOCK_IN_FUTURE. The latest date you can lock is yesterday, Pakistan time, and the message names that date.
- Failures are flagged: completeOrder calls the new postCompletionOrFlag, and the refund/cancel path calls postRefundOrFlag. The order's loyalty earn is checked by ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked, which posts it if it is missing. Any refusal raises one open, high-severity 'posting_failed' exception. It carries the order id, the posting type, the reason and the order's company (helpers flagPostingFailed / resolvePostingFailed in journal.ts; a second refusal does not add a second flag).
- Backfill: POST /reconciliation/backfill-unposted also runs the new backfillUnpostedOrders, per company in the caller's scope.
  - Order completions are re-posted when the order is completed or refunded, its completion actually ran (or it has an open flag), and it has no entry.
  - Loyalty earns and redemptions that were never reversed and have no entry are re-posted, earns first.
  - Refund restores that were flagged are re-run through the existing postOrderRefund.
  - It is a dry run by default and is safe to run twice. A posting dated inside a closed period is listed as 'locked' and never posted. A posting that lands resolves its flag.
  - The response keeps the shift rows and summary as before and adds an `orders` field with its own rows and summary.

(2) BOOKS-06: postJournalEntry refuses any line above 2,147,483,647 paisa with 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE: 'split this amount into lines of at most PKR 21,474,836.47'. That one check covers every posting path. POST /accounting/journal checks first, before anything else runs. The manual-journal review flag (and the reversal flag) used to fail silently when the total was above the same limit; the amount now goes in metadata so the flag still saves. No schema change.

(3) BOH-R2-02:
- At posting: postSupplierBill now prices the variance only on min(billed, received-to-date minus what other live bills on that PO line already matched). Of that, the stock still on hand is re-costed and the stock already used goes to 5060. The rest is carried in 1210 until it arrives. It locks the PO rows first, the same order receiving uses.
- Record: what each line absorbed, used and carried is saved as an accounting audit row ('supplier.bill.variance') on the bill. Each later receipt adds a 'supplier.bill.variance_applied' row via the new exported applyCarriedBillVarianceTx.
- Void: the void takes back out of stock exactly what the bill put in and is still there (each part less the share of its stock used since). It no longer re-derives a share from today's stock. 5060 trues up the rest. Bills posted before this change keep the old void logic.

Tests: new tests/resimBooks.test.ts, all passing. It includes two-company checks and checks that every entry balances inside its own company's chart. In the chicken repro the cost returns to 950 (within 1 paisa) and 5060 nets to rounding (under PKR 1) instead of PKR 600. In the never-received case nothing goes to 5060 and the stock on hand is not re-priced. The existing BOH-13 tests pass unchanged.

items.note: Locking: the latest lockable date is yesterday (PKT); today and later get 422 LOCK_IN_FUTURE naming yesterday (accounting/routes.ts). Flagging: refused order.complete, order.refund (wallet / gift-card / loyalty restores) and the order's loyalty.earn each raise one open high 'posting_failed' flag in the order's company, with the order id and the reason (orders/service.ts postCompletionOrFlag / postRefundOrFlag / ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked). Backfill: /reconciliation/backfill-unposted re-posts missing order.complete, loyalty.earn / loyalty.redeem and flagged refund restores. It runs per company, is a dry run by default, and is safe to run twice. Postings dated inside a lock are listed as 'locked' and not posted. Landed postings resolve their flags. Tested end to end: a lock through today was inserted straight into the table (a lock that may already exist in prod). Each company's order was flagged in its own company, A's run never lists or posts B's rows, and output tax 19,500 / revenue 130,000 land in A's books after the reopen.

This is the 422 guard planned for Monday; the real fix, a BigInt migration, is not done. Every posting path is guarded in postJournalEntry (MAX_LINE_CENTS = INT4 max), with 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE 'split this amount into lines of at most PKR 21,474,836.47'. POST /accounting/journal checks first. A PKR 25m opening balance gets the 422; the same amount split into lines of 12.5m posts. The manual-JE review flag (and the reversal flag) used to fail silently when the total was above INT4; the total now goes in metadata so the flag saves. No schema change; see prodNotes.

The variance now applies only to min(billed, received-to-date minus what other live bills matched). The used part goes to 5060 and the unreceived part is carried in 1210. What was absorbed, used and carried is stored in accounting audit rows (no schema change). A void takes back exactly what is still in stock and trues up 5060 for the rest. Carried variance reaches the item's cost on receipt through the exported applyCarriedBillVarianceTx, which receiving.ts must call (see needsOtherFiles). Until it does, the carried amount sits in 1210 and a void reverses it cleanly.

review.title: Running backfill-unposted twice at once posts every order.complete and loyalty.earn twice
review.scenario: Reproduced in /home/user/servd/backend/.sim/review-b/reviewB.test.ts ('backfill run twice at once'; DB servd_test_rf_b_rv, Redis 6390/13). Setup: lock company A through today, complete 8 online orders (each is flagged), remove the lock, then send two POST /reconciliation/backfill-unposted {dryRun:false} at the same time. Two tabs, a double-click or two CEOs would do this. Both calls return 200, and every order has 2 'order.complete:<id>' entries: counts [2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]. All 8 'loyalty.earn:<tx>' entries are also duplicated. Revenue, output GST (2030/2032) and 2060 are therefore booked twice, and the SRB/FBR return overstates against the fiscal POS. The cause is in postJournalEntry: its idempotency is a findFirst followed by a create, inside a READ COMMITTED transaction, with no unique index on journal_entries.reference and no lock. The backfill is a new bulk path that races itself, and it can also race the in-flight async postCompletionOrFlag of an order completed seconds earlier.
review.fix: In journal.ts postJournalEntry run(), take a transaction-scoped lock on the reference before the existing-entry check: `await tx.$executeRaw`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(${input.tenantId}), hashtext(${idempotencyRef}))``. That serialises every posting path on (company, reference), so the second caller finds the first entry. Also make the route single-flight per company: pg_try_advisory_lock on the tenant id, and answer 409 BACKFILL_RUNNING when the lock is held. Add a test that fires two concurrent real runs and asserts each reference has exactly one entry.

review.title: A bill voided after its stock was used and restocked still re-prices the new stock below the PO price (the BOH-R2-02 symptom remains)
review.scenario: Reproduced in .sim/review-b/reviewB.test.ts ('void after the billed stock was used and replenished'). Chicken PO of 20 @ 95,000. Receive 10, then bill 10 @ 100,000: cost re-averages to 100,000 (absorbed 50,000, onHandAtPosting 10). The kitchen uses all 10 (COGS at 1,000/kg), then the next 10 arrive at 95,000, so cost is 95,000. Voiding the bill drops the cost to 90,000/kg, below any price paid, and 5060 nets to 0. postSupplierBillVoid sets stillInStock = slice × min(1, onHandNow / onHandAtPosting), which is 1, so it takes the whole 50,000 out of stock bought later at the right price, and trueUp = 50,000 − 50,000 = 0. The correct result is: stock stays at 95,000, and Dr 1210 / Cr 5060 50,000 gives back the variance that was consumed. Restaurant stock turns over daily and a void usually comes days later, so this is the common case. It contradicts the builder's claim that the void 'takes back exactly what is still there'.
review.fix: Estimate the part of each slice still on hand without counting stock received after the slice: stillQty = clamp(onHandNow − (quantity received into the item since the slice's timestamp, from goods-receipt lines / PO-line receipts and any other stock-in), 0, slice.onHand). Then stillInStock = slice.cents × stillQty / slice.onHand. This is FIFO: newer receipts are what is on hand. Store the slice's createdAt (it is already on the audit rows) and use it. Add the used-then-restocked regression above, asserting cost 95,000 and 5060 −50,000 on the void.

review.title: The carried variance never reaches item cost: receiving.ts does not call applyCarriedBillVarianceTx, so 1210 and stock valuation drift apart
review.scenario: In the current tree, no production code calls applyCarriedBillVarianceTx. Only resimBooks.test.ts calls it, by hand, after receiveGoods, so the suite passes without the hook. Real flow: receive 40 of 60, then bill 60 @ +PKR 50/kg. The bill debits 1210 with the full subtotal and carries 20 × 5,000 = 100,000. The last 20 kg arrive at the PO cost and the carried amount is never applied. 1210 stays 100,000 above Σ stock × cost for good, and the item cost stays understated. A later bill on the same PO line also counts those 20 kg as unmatched (matchedByOtherBills only adds receivedQty plus the applied rows, and there are no applied rows), so it re-prices them again. BOH-R2-02 is only half fixed unless the receiving change lands in the same release.
review.fix: Land the hook described in needsOtherFiles in the same change: in receiveGoods' transaction, after the PurchaseOrderLine quantityReceived increment, `if (l.quantityReceived > 0) await applyCarriedBillVarianceTx(tx, { poLineId: l.poLineId, quantity: l.quantityReceived, supplierId: supplier.id })`. Change resimBooks.test.ts to stop calling it by hand and assert that the carried variance lands on the receipt.

review.title: Two lines of one bill on the same PO line both match the same received kilos
review.scenario: Reproduced in .sim/review-b/reviewB.test.ts ('one bill, two lines on the same PO line'). Beef PO of 20 @ 180,000; receive 10. One bill has two lines of 10 @ 190,000 on that PO line. Both records come out as receivedQty 10 / carriedQty 0 / absorbed 100,000, and the 10 kg on hand is priced at 200,000/kg instead of 190,000, with nothing carried. matchedByOtherBills excludes the bill's own id, so line 2 never subtracts what line 1 has just matched. Until the other 10 kg arrive, recipe cost and COGS run 100,000 high on that stock. Later bills on the line also see 20 matched against 10 received.
review.fix: In postSupplierBill, keep a running Map<poLineId, matchedSoFar> across the bill's own variance lines. Compute available = quantityReceived − matchedByOtherBills − matchedSoFar, then add receivedQty to the map.

review.title: A bill void racing a receipt can leave carried variance in item cost after 1210 has been reversed (once the receiving hook lands)
review.scenario: postSupplierBillVoid locks only the supplier_bills row. It reads the applied records before revalueItem takes the item lock. Receiving locks purchase_orders and then the item, and applyCarriedBillVarianceTx reads the bill status without a lock. Concurrently, the void reads 'no applied slices', and the receipt (still seeing the bill as posted) applies the carried variance to the cost and commits. The void then reverses the whole bill out of 1210 but only takes the posting-time slice out of stock, so stock is overvalued against 1210 by the carried amount.
review.fix: In postSupplierBillVoid, after the bill lock and before varianceRecordsOf, lock the bill's purchase orders in the same order postSupplierBill uses: `SELECT id FROM purchase_orders WHERE id = ANY(<po ids of the bill's lines>) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE`. In applyCarriedBillVarianceTx, also re-read the bill status after receiving's PO lock (the PO lock already serialises it with the void).

review.title: A loyalty.earn posting_failed flag stays open for good once the earn is reversed
review.scenario: Earn refused under a lock: ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked opens a high 'loyalty.earn' flag on the Order. The order is then cancelled or refunded, and postOrderRefund claims the earn (reversedAt set; the reversal returns original_not_booked, which is correct because the books net to zero). The backfill's loyalty query requires reversedAt IS NULL, so it never visits that earn and never resolves the flag. The CEO's inbox keeps a high 'did not reach the ledger (2060)' flag for something that needs no posting, and the backfill cannot clear it.
review.fix: In the backfill, resolve open loyalty.earn / loyalty.redeem posting_failed flags whose transaction now has reversedAt set (resolution: 'Reversed before it was booked — nothing to post'). Alternatively, resolve them in postOrderRefund when postLoyaltyReversal returns original_not_booked.

fix.summary:
I fixed all six review findings in stream B's files, with regression tests. RB-3 also needs a one-line hook in procurement/receiving.ts, which I don't own (exact change under needsOtherFiles). Until that lands, its test is the one failure in resimBooks.

RB-1: postJournalEntry now takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock on (company, reference) before its "already posted?" check. Every posting path is serialised per company and reference, so racing callers find the first entry instead of writing a second. The route is also single-flight per company: a second real run for a company already running gets 409 BACKFILL_RUNNING. That guard is an in-process Set, not pg_try_advisory_lock, because a session advisory lock leaks across pooled Prisma connections; the posting lock is what keeps the books right across processes. Dry runs are never blocked.

RB-2: when a bill is voided, stock received after the bill's price change is no longer counted as the stock it re-priced. For each priced slice, the part still on hand is on-hand now minus goods received since the slice (excluding the slice's own receipt), capped at what the slice was spread over. The rest goes back through 5060. In the reviewer's case (bill priced 10 kg, kitchen used them, next 10 kg came at the PO price), cost now stays 95,000 and the void posts Dr 1210 / Cr 5060 50,000. Only goods receipts count as stock arriving.

RB-4: postSupplierBill keeps a running total per PO line of what the bill's own earlier lines matched, so two lines on one PO line no longer match the same received kilos. Two related fixes: applying carried variance on receipt now works through a bill's record lines in order (before, a second carried line on the same PO line was never applied), and the void groups slices per PO line so applied slices aren't counted twice.

RB-5: postSupplierBillVoid locks the bill's purchase orders (sorted) right after the bill lock, before reading what the bill applied. That is the same order postSupplierBill and receiving use. applyCarriedBillVarianceTx also takes the PO lock itself and reads bill status after it. It now accepts an optional receiptId, stored on the applied record, and is idempotent per receipt.

RB-6: the backfill has a new step that resolves open loyalty.earn / loyalty.redeem posting_failed flags in the caller's companies when the transaction was reversed before it was booked ("Reversed before it was booked — nothing to post."), was booked since, or no longer exists. A dry run lists these as would_resolve; nothing posts.

Rejected: nothing; all six were confirmed. Not changed in orders/service.ts.

items.note: journal.ts: per-(company, reference) advisory lock before the existing-entry check. Route: in-process single-flight per company, 409 BACKFILL_RUNNING. Tested with 10 concurrent postJournalEntry calls (one entry; company B separate) and two concurrent engine runs (each order.complete and loyalty.earn once). Two concurrent route calls give 200 plus 200 or 409, and B's run is never blocked by A's.

supplierPosting.ts void: still on hand = on-hand now minus goods received since the slice, capped at the slice's stock (new receivedSince helper). Tests: the reviewer's used-then-restocked case (cost 95,000, 5060 −50,000, 1210 +50,000) and a partly-used case.

The fix is in receiving.ts, which I don't own (exact hook in needsOtherFiles). On my side, applyCarriedBillVarianceTx takes receiptId, is idempotent per receipt and takes the PO lock itself. resimBooks now has the test 'RB-3: receiving applies the carried variance by itself (no manual call)', which fails until the hook lands. The other tests' helper only bridges by hand while receiving.ts lacks the call (it checks the source), and the bridge is idempotent.

Running per-PO-line total of what the bill's own lines matched. Also fixed: carried variance now applies to a second record line on the same PO line, and the void groups slices per PO line. Test: records [[10,0],[0,10]], cost 190,000; after the rest arrives it stays 190,000; void returns 180,000 with no leftover 5060.

Void locks the bill's POs (sorted) before reading applied records; applyCarriedBillVarianceTx takes the PO lock and reads bill status after it. Test holds a receipt transaction open with the carried variance applied, checks the void waits, then that the void takes the slice back (cost 150,000, 5060 0).

New backfill step resolves loyalty flags whose transaction was reversed unbooked, has since been booked, or no longer exists. Test: earn refused under a lock, order cancelled, B's run leaves A's flag open, A's dry run shows would_resolve, A's real run resolves it, nothing posted.

fix.needsOtherFiles:
backend/src/modules/procurement/receiving.ts (RB-3, needed in the same release):
1. Add `import { applyCarriedBillVarianceTx } from '../accounting/supplierPosting.js'`.
2. In receiveGoods' prisma.$transaction, inside `for (const l of prepared)`, change the block that increments PurchaseOrderLine.quantityReceived to:
```
if (l.quantityReceived > 0) {
  await tx.purchaseOrderLine.update({ where: { id: l.poLineId }, data: { quantityReceived: { increment: l.quantityReceived } } })
  await applyCarriedBillVarianceTx(tx, { poLineId: l.poLineId, quantity: l.quantityReceived, supplierId: supplier.id, receiptId: receipt.id })
}
```
The PO is already locked, the PO line and stock are updated, and `receipt` exists at that point. When this lands, the 'RB-3: receiving applies the carried variance by itself' test in resimBooks passes, and the suite's helper stops bridging by hand on its own (it checks receiving.ts for the call).
fix.prodNotes:
The posting lock serialises every postJournalEntry on (company, reference). It is released at commit. A caller that posts several references in one transaction in varying order could in theory hit a Postgres deadlock error (retryable), but no current path does that.

The backfill single-flight guard is per API process; correctness across processes comes from the posting lock.

A void's "received since" counts goods receipts only. A stock count that raised stock is not treated as a delivery.

Edge race not fixed, because it is in loyaltyPosting.ts (not owned): a backfill can post an earn after a concurrent refund has already claimed it and returned original_not_booked, leaving a booked earn that is never reversed. Closing it needs postLoyaltyEarn to refuse an earn whose reversedAt is set. Narrow window, low priority.

Stream K is done: BOH-R2-01 and BOH-R2-04 are fixed. R2-UI-02 is fixed for reading only: the buyer can now open the receiving page, but still cannot take a delivery in, because of owner decision 27.

**Expo Fire and course pacing (BOH-R2-01).** An earlier attempt left most of this in place in backend/src/modules/expo/routes.ts; I reviewed it and finished it.
- Fire now starts only the course's lines whose fire time is empty or already passed. The shorter dishes stay pending, the pacing worker fires them on time, and the response lists them as `paced: [{id, name, scheduledFireAt}]`.
- An order paid at the till first is paced the same way.
- A plain second Fire no longer sends a paced dish early.
- I closed a race: the schedule is now re-set from the moment of Fire *before* the order moves to 'preparing'. Before, a creation-time schedule that had expired could let the 30-second pacing worker fire the whole course in that gap. If re-setting the schedule fails, it is logged rather than failing the request.
- "Fire all now" (`fireAll: true`) is the override. Only managers and the expediter can use it (others get 403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED), it writes an `expo.fire_all` audit entry, and it also works on an order already fired. Company separation is unchanged: another company's order is 404.
- The expo queue now returns `scheduledFireAt` on each line.
- Admin /expo shows "<dish> fires at 14:59" under In Progress orders, a notice after Fire, and a "Fire all now" button for managers and the expediter. The tablet expo ticket shows "Fries · fires at 14:59".

**Prep batch company check (BOH-R2-04).** In backend/src/modules/crosschecks/routes.ts the recipe is now checked against the active company's sub-recipes (`subRecipeIdsForCompany`, the same list the par sheet and prep page offer). Another company's sub-recipe, a plate recipe or an unknown id now gets 422 RECIPE_NOT_IN_COMPANY, and no batch is stored and no stock moves. I also removed the `inputs as never` cast on that database write.

**Receiving page for the buyer (R2-UI-02).** GET /crosschecks/receiving, /receiving/suppliers and /receiving/open-pos now admit the procurement role, scoped to their company exactly as for managers. POST /crosschecks/receiving stays managers-only. The task asked to open it too, but the verifier showed that owner decision 27 deliberately keeps receiving away from whoever raised the PO; it is in the code comments, procurement/receiving.ts and receiving.test.ts. So the buyer can read the page but still gets 403 when submitting a delivery.

items.note: Fire now starts only the lines that are due. Shorter dishes stay pending, come back as `paced` with their fire time, and the pacing worker fires them. The schedule is re-set before the order leaves 'received', which closes the gap where the worker could fire everything at once. A paid-first till sale is paced too. 'Fire all now' (`fireAll: true`) is limited to managers and the expediter (403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED for others) and audited. The queue returns `scheduledFireAt`, and admin /expo and the tablet expo ticket show 'fires at HH:MM'. Another company's order is 404.

The recipe id must be one of the active company's sub-recipes (subRecipeIdsForCompany), otherwise 422 RECIPE_NOT_IN_COMPANY with no batch stored and no stock drawn. The company's own sub-recipe still records yield without drawing stock, and a batch with no recipe still draws. I also removed the `as never` cast on the inputs write.

Read-only fix. The 3 receiving GETs now admit the procurement role, scoped to their company. POST /crosschecks/receiving stays managers-only, per owner decision 27 (whoever raises a PO does not receive it), as the verifier advised; the task text asked to open it too. The admin page still needs to hide its submit form from the buyer (see needsOtherFiles).

review.title: The 'Fire all now' role limit can be bypassed: any staff role can fire paced dishes early through POST /orders/:id/fire-course
review.scenario: Reproduced on servd_test_rf_k_rv with the stream's fixture (Classic 8 min, Fries 3 min). The expediter presses Fire: Classic starts and Fries comes back in `paced` with a fire time 5 minutes later. A line cook (role kitchen) then sends POST /expo/orders/:id/fire {fireAll:true} and correctly gets 403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED. The same cook then sends POST /orders/:id/fire-course {course:1} and gets 200 {fired:1}, and Fries goes to 'preparing' 5 minutes early. No expo.fire_all audit row is written. /orders is gated on modules that kitchen (kds_dashboard), cashier and foh all hold, so the claim that only managers and the expediter can override pacing does not hold. The admin /orders/[id]/courses page shows a 'Fire course →' button for course 1 while the order is still 'received'. That button fires the whole course at once with no pacing and leaves the order in 'received'.
review.fix: This is outside the stream's files (needsOtherFiles). In orders/service.ts fireCourse, or in the fire-course route, treat the order's first course the way expo Fire now does: fire only lines whose scheduledFireAt is null or already past. A paced line should fire only when a FIRE_ALL_ROLES caller sends an explicit override, and that override should be audited. Alternatively, refuse fire-course for course 1 and send expo to POST /expo/orders/:id/fire. Add a test: the line cook's fire-course on course 1 leaves Fries pending.

review.title: A till sale paid after its creation-time schedule has expired is still fired all at once by the pacing worker. The re-anchor only runs on expo's path
review.scenario: Reproduced. createPosOrder creates the order as 'received' with Classic + Fries, and the creation-time pacing sets Classic to now and Fries to now+5m. The order then waits about 10 minutes before payment, simulated by moving scheduledFireAt into the past. Expo does not fire it in that time. processPayment moves it from received to completed, and that path does not re-anchor (transitionOrder re-anchors only on received→confirmed or preparing). PACING_FIRED includes 'completed', so the next processCoursePacingTick fires both lines in the same tick: Classic and Fries both 'preparing' with the same firedAt (07:19:54.009Z). This is the expired-schedule race the builder says is closed, but it is closed only for received→preparing. It is also why 'an order paid at the till first is paced the same way' holds only when payment comes within the shortest pace gap of ring-up. Counter sales where the card machine or bill splitting takes a few minutes are exactly this case.
review.fix: In orders/service.ts (completeOrder / the till_payment path, or processCoursePacingTick), when a till sale leaves 'received' by payment and none of its first-course lines has fired yet, await scheduleCoursePacing(orderId) before the order becomes eligible for the worker. Alternatively, have the worker re-anchor such an order before firing and then fire only the lines that are due. Add a test: ring up, expire the times, pay, run a tick. Only Classic should fire and Fries should get a fresh time about 5 minutes out.

review.title: The expo.fire_all audit row is stamped with the operator's active company instead of the order's company
review.scenario: The fire route looks up the order with scopeTenantWhere(req,'write'), which covers every company the operator belongs to. A manager who belongs to companies A and B, with A active, presses 'Fire all now' on a company B order. The audit row is written with tenantId = req.staffUser.tenantId (A), so B's audit trail is missing the override and A's shows an order that is not A's. CLAUDE.md requires every record to take its company from the source document.
review.fix: Select concept.tenantId on the order lookup (or resolve it from order.conceptId) and pass that as the audit tenantId in place of req.staffUser!.tenantId. Add a two-company test in which an operator in both companies, with A active, fire-alls B's order and the audit row carries tenantB.

1) K-RV-01, in backend/src/modules/orders/service.ts fireCourse(orderId, course): when `course` is the order's FIRST course (the lowest courseOf over its live lines, as in scheduleCoursePacing), also select scheduledFireAt. Fire only lines where `scheduledFireAt == null || scheduledFireAt <= now` (a paced line is left to processCoursePacingTick). Return the rest as `paced`. Later courses are unchanged.
   Optionally, give fireCourse an `opts?: { fireAll?: boolean }` parameter. In backend/src/modules/orders/routes.ts POST /:id/fire-course, accept `fireAll?: boolean` and allow it only for roles [...MANAGERS, 'expediter'] (otherwise 403 FIRE_ALL_NOT_ALLOWED, same as expo). Audit it as action 'expo.fire_all' with tenantId = the order's concept.tenantId.
   The route currently answers 404 NO_ITEMS when nothing fired. When only paced lines remain, prefer 409 PACED (or a 200 that includes `paced`) so the admin /orders/[id]/courses button doesn't read as "not found".
   Simpler alternative: refuse course 1 here when the order is 'received' and send expo to POST /expo/orders/:id/fire.
   When this lands, change `pendingOther(` to `it(` for the K-RV-01 test in backend/tests/resimKitchen.test.ts. The test registers orderCourseRoutes at /orders. It expects that a cook's fire-course on course 1 after expo Fire leaves Fries 'pending' and writes no expo.fire_all row.
2) K-RV-02, in backend/src/modules/orders/service.ts processCoursePacingTick: after grouping `due` by order (byOrder), for each order whose FIRST course has no line out of 'pending' and no firedAt (nothing of the first course has started), first `await scheduleCoursePacing(orderId)`. Then re-read those ids' scheduledFireAt and pass only the ones still <= now to fireOrderItems. The re-anchor puts the longest dish at now and pushes the shorter ones to now + (maxLabor − labor) minutes.
   This covers every route by which a till sale leaves 'received' (cash, card, split bill, group bill) without hooking each payment path.
   Alternative: in completeOrder's till-payment path, when the order leaves 'received' and none of its first-course lines has fired, await scheduleCoursePacing(orderId) before it commits as 'completed'.
   When this lands, change `pendingOther(` to `it(` for the K-RV-02 test in resimKitchen.test.ts. That test rings up, expires the times, pays, runs one tick, and expects Classic 'preparing' and Fries 'pending' with a fire time more than 4 minutes out.
fix.ownerQuestions: Should POST /orders/:id/fire-course stay as a second way to fire course 1? Or should course 1 always go through expo's Fire, with fire-course kept for later courses only (and the admin /orders/[id]/courses button hidden for course 1 while the order is 'received')? The two options are equivalent for the K-RV-01 fix, but removing the duplicate path matches the "no two sources of truth" rule.
fix.prodNotes: The expo.fire_all audit row now carries the order's company. Fire-all rows written before this change in a multi-company session may carry the operator's active company instead.
